newsitem.title: FRANCE: New sugar contract performance pleases MATIF.
newsitem.headline: New sugar contract performance pleases MATIF.

text.p: MATIF's new 100-Icumsa sugar contract has attracted average daily volume of 221 lots since its launch on June 20 -- a performance the French futures exchange described on Wednesday as "encouraging".
In a statement, the exchange said total trade on the contract between June 20 and June 30 was 1,547 lots. Open positions at end June stood at 1,148.

"These first results are encouraging and confirm clients are interested in having access to a variety of contracts and options on white sugar which they can use as hedging tools...(and) for arbitrage play between the 45 and 100 Icumsa contracts," MATIF said.
MATIF has not given a volume target for the new contract.
MATIF has said the new contract represents lesser quality sugar that better matches world trade flows than the 45 Icumsa.
Icumsa (International Commisson for Uniform Method of Sugar Analysis) ratings measure the colouring of sugar and are an indication of quality,
Sugar with ratings of 100 Icumsa is produced mostly in South America, Central America and Asia and currently accounts for over a third of world trade.

MATIF statistics for June also showed total volume for the old-style 45 Icumsa contract was 12,055 lots with an average 574 lots traded daily. Open positions at end June reached 6,955 lot. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
